approachQuestion.prompt: Return every suffix total. Given n signed charges (1 <= n <= 100,000), return an array where result[i] is the sum from charges[i] through the last element. Example: charges=[5,-2,4] returns [7,2,4]. Choose a method that produces all answers without keeping a second full table of partial results.
constraints: The result array is required output and is excluded from auxiliary-space accounting.
Each total fits in signed 64-bit; input is read-only.

options.text: Walk from right to left, keep one running total, and write that total to the corresponding output position.
options.feedback: The next suffix is formed by adding one value to the suffix already seen, so only one running total must stay live.

options.text: Build a separate array of all suffix totals, then copy it into the returned result.
options.feedback: The totals are correct, but the separate full table is unnecessary because each result can be written as soon as its running total is known.

options.text: Walk left to right and write the running prefix total at each position.
options.feedback: This returns prefix totals, not suffix totals. For [5,-2,4] it produces [5,3,7] instead of [7,2,4].

options.text: For each output position, start a new sum over that position through the end.
options.feedback: The answers are correct, but repeated suffix scans revisit most values many times; for n=100,000 it revisits values already included in earlier suffix totals.

feedback.reason: The direction of traversal lets one answer build directly on the next without storing intermediate answers separately.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Choose the time and auxiliary-space pair for reverse-running-suffix. The returned result array is output, not auxiliary space.
constraints: The algorithm allocates the required result array and one running total.

feedback.reason: Each charge is read once and each result slot is written once. Beyond the required output, only the running total and index are retained.

methodReveal.title: Accumulate from the end
methodReveal.description: Initialize a running total to zero. Visit indices from n-1 down to zero, add the current charge, and write the running total into result[i]. The input is preserved, and no separate table of partial sums is needed.
